# Go upstream protocol and authentication campaign

Independent audit correction (same campaign): the 83-case execution text is historical evidence for that selection. [The inventory audit](upstream-inventory-audit.md) corrects individual mappings below and adds distinct public cases; it does not claim the source functions or old suite were fully executed.

This is the Go allocation of the second upstream campaign (2026-11-08).
It surveys **every actual `*_test.go` in all five pinned trees**, including
portable-smb-server's separate `test/go.mod` and nested rig, plus client integration
suites. Repository names do not determine server applicability: macos-fuse-t,
sonroyaalmerol and portable-smb-server are servers; CloudSoda and hirochachacha are
clients. No upstream product code or Go dependency is added to ordinary builds.

The updated user scope includes observable NTLM/SPNEGO/session/signing behavior
and excludes new adaptations that only test implementation internals. Consequently
this inventory distinguishes internal encoder/crypto/cache/API tests from protocol
facets translated into actual requests. An internal test's source row is retained;
it is never called a passing server test. No production source was edited.

## Maintained cases and independent oracles

`UpstreamGoTests.Cases()` registers the cases from `UpstreamGoTests.cs`,
`UpstreamGoExtraTests.cs` and `UpstreamGoAuthTests.cs` under `upstream.go.`.
All filesystem cases use authenticated signed TCP against the real LocalFileStore;
backend bytes corroborate wire effects. Authentication cases use a separate raw
TCP client, literal SMB layouts, independent HMAC-MD5/HMAC-SHA256 and a small RC4
implementation feeding actual type-3 packets. The NTOWFv2 known-answer key
`0c868a403bfd7a93a3001ef22ef02e3f` is from the pinned NTLM tests for
Password/User/Domain. No production NTLM builder/verifier forms their oracle.
Signing-required/default authentication configuration is retained; dedicated required-encryption cases strengthen that policy. Optional-encryption cases retain the default policy and voluntarily encrypt every post-auth packet. A raw handshake
and SPNEGO handshake each finish with independently verified signed ECHO,
TREE_CONNECT, CREATE and CLOSE. Helper algorithms are not standalone tests.

| Local suffix / group | Protocol behavior and rows |
|---|---|
| `io.sequential-truncate`, `io.sequential-model` | Go TestFile's exact `test` + `Content` writes, 11-byte stat, shrink-to-4 and `est` short read; the 18 literal model operations plus 32 bounded deterministic model operations. Seek selects wire offsets, not a fictitious SMB seek command. Go PCG implementation/offset accessors are not copied. |
| `io.mutate-append-shrink-grow-hole` | Original 3MiB seed, append 1MiB, overwrite 300KiB at 1MiB, shrink 2621440, grow 6MiB, append 300KiB, write 1MiB at 8MiB; independent complete bytes and live EOF after each step, including zero-filled holes. |
| `io.random-access-64mib` | Original `(offsetMiB,lengthMiB)` rows `(0,1),(13,2),(31,1),(63,1),(40,8),(5,3)`. |
| `io.large-stream-256mib`, `io.sparse-4-5gib` | Original matrix transfer scale with bounded 60KiB requests and SHA256; 4.5GiB EOF, tail at 4607MiB and zero-filled 1MiB range at 2048MiB. Sparse EOF does not assert physical allocated blocks or power-loss durability. |
| `io.positioned-concurrent`, `io.truncate-peer-live-eof`, `io.truncate-invalid-preserves` | Eight disjoint 32KiB I/O lanes over independent sessions; live peer EOF after shrink/grow/zero; signed negative length rejection and valid retry (only if rejection succeeds). |
| `io.append-truncate-and-copy`, `io.buffered-copy-model` | Append/truncate false/true with A/B/C; copy at queried EOF; exact long-tail/source-EOF/reuse-after-seek model rows. ReadFrom versus WriteTo wrappers collapse to identical packets. |
| `io.copy-offsets-and-tail` | CopyOnly, actual resume-key plus COPYCHUNK, seven distinct offset pairs `(0,0),(4,4),(4,0),(0,6),(4,6),(3,5),(8,16)`, source preservation and exact destination bytes. Append-equal/different client wrappers reduce to existing offset rows, not extra tests. |
| `names.unicode-punctuation-long`, `names.mixed-separators-spaces` | All portable matrix name rows, additional umlaut filename, 200 ASCII/60 Japanese character components, emoji surrogate pair, directory spaces/Japanese and mixed slashes. No Windows-illegal unencoded names. |
| `names.deep-tree-22`, `names.remove-tree-postorder` | Original 22 levels with listings at levels 1/11/22 and leaf; three-leaf nested tree removed with explicit postorder SMB operations. Recursive RemoveAll itself is client-only. |
| `names.case-only-rename`, `names.directory-rename-live-child`, `names.cross-directory-move` | Case-preserving single surviving name; renamed subtree with usable child FileId and reopen; cross-directory relocation and exact old/new name sets. Native macOS/Windows client cache shortcuts are not required server behavior. |
| `enum.create-list-delete-1000`, `enum.5000-and-300-lookups` | Original 1000 creates and deletes with representative reads; original 5000 host-seeded names, exact paged set/no duplicates/termination and 300 network-open stats. Wall-clock performance comparisons are not counted as protocol conformance. |
| `enum.parallel-50`, `enum.churn-300` | 50 independent cursors with exact stable sets; 300 create/write/rename/delete operations while another session enumerates, bounded deterministic rounds, then exact empty backing. Active-scan membership is unspecified. |
| `enum.layout-1/2/3/37/38` | Five distinct FSCC layouts: Directory/Full/Both/IdBoth/IdFull. Independent fixed/name offsets, UTF16 byte lengths, aligned bounded next-entry offsets, EOF/type and opaque IDs. `.`/`..` are legal optional entries and client-filtered. |
| `metadata.create-directory-readonly` | Requested DIRECTORY and READONLY CREATE flags must survive the response and FileBasicInformation query. No owner-write/POSIX ACL projection is asserted. |
| `names.open-if-existing-readonly` | Read/attributes-only OPEN_IF of an existing readonly file preserves data/attributes; it must not require OS write access. |
| `ioctl.response-buffer-offset-relation` | Actual resume-key IOCTL response output must start at aligned InputOffset+InputCount even when InputCount is zero; reserved flags and FileId echo are also checked when the earlier relation succeeds. |
| `metadata.network-open-live`, `metadata.chtimes`, `metadata.chmod-readonly`, `metadata.file-id-survives-rename` | NetworkOpenInformation 56-byte layout/EOF, fixed 2006 timestamps, readonly attribute set/clear and stable opaque file identity with old-name recreation. No full POSIX permission, pathname-derived ID or timestamp durability claim. |
| `concurrent.readers-8`, `concurrent.writers-8`, `concurrent.sessions-50`, `concurrent.publish-rename-delete-visibility` | Original eight 8MiB readers/writers and 50 sessions; peer immediately sees write/publication by rename/deletion without retry loops. Native OS mount/cache behavior remains a platform blocker. |
| `disconnect.partial-transfer-recovery`, `routing.share-isolation` | Transport loss after an unfinished application transfer with an unclosed FileId, bounded resource retirement, delete and subsequent I/O; two authenticated trees route to distinct backends. This is not a claim of killing a native OS client mid-physical-write. |
| `protocol.enumerate-regular-file` | QUERY_DIRECTORY against a regular-file FileId rejects INVALID_PARAMETER without affecting the readable file. |
| `close.postquery-0/1`, `protocol.unknown-set-info`, `io.readonly-handle-denies-write` | Optional CLOSE fields absent/present and final metadata; invalid SET_INFO class; readonly handle WRITE rejection with data preserved. DELETE_ON_CLOSE-specific suppression in portable upstream is a server policy, not imposed as normative SMB behavior. |
| `readonly.*` | Eight mutations: write-open/new-file/mkdir/delete-on-close/write/rename/delete/truncate, ACCESS_DENIED is the supported local rejection; portable's exact MEDIA_WRITE_PROTECTED choice is not imposed. Creation gaps remain RED. Advertisement policy differs normatively, as explained in the final findings. |
| `auth.ntlm.*` | raw/SPNEGO/keyexchange/MIC success, exact pinned SPNEGO initial negotiate vector and literal accept-incomplete/accept-completed state assertions; wrong password/user/domain, tampered proof/MIC, missing announced MIC, short proof, truncated/overflowed authenticate buffers. Failure cannot establish a usable session. |
| `auth.initial.*` | Empty/garbage/truncated-SPNEGO/unsupported-Kerberos-mechanism, followed by a new valid exchange on the same channel. |
| `auth.integrity.*`, `auth.challenge-replay`, `auth.logoff-retires-key`, `auth.framing.fragmented-ntlm` | Tampered payload/signature/unsigned required-signing/cross-session key rejection; challenge replay fails while original context succeeds; logoff retires old SessionId; byte-fragmented framing survives an entire independent NTLM handshake. |

Expected results follow the pinned upstream packet/FS scenarios and the public
[MS-SMB2 command contracts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-smb2/)
and [MS-FSCC information layouts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-fscc/).
Upstream shortcuts are not normative: no pathname-based FileId, POSIX immediate
unlink, universal case folding, all-IPC-CREATE rejection, forced completion ordering,
truncated fixed FSCC records or delete-close attribute suppression is imported.

## Execution and failure evidence

Runtime evidence is external in the new campaign's `go/` directory; filenames below
are relative to that directory. There are no maintained storage-mount literals.
`logs/build-first.log` retains the initial compile error (one owned span/await bug
and concurrently edited Microsoft files); `build-second.log` is the clean first
build. `logs/first-run.log` records **44/59** before fixture corrections.
The enumeration fixture incorrectly assumed SUCCESS on alternating exhausted
pages and counted legal dot entries as user files. Those are fixture errors, not
production fixes: it now validates each response, terminates on proper status and
filters only `.`/`..`, preserving exact real-name/count/layout expectations.
`logs/fixture-corrected-run.log` records **58/59**. No expectation was weakened to
match production. The concurrent first-open failure occurred in first-run and again
in complete-run despite passing the intervening run; it remains a finding.
`logs/complete-run.log` records **70/74** before the two read-only advertisement
extensions. Final-source results and diagnoses are appended below.

External evidence: `interop-client` builds from pinned CloudSoda with isolated
Go module/toolchain caches. `logs/external-go-client.log` passes a fresh signed
NTLM/CREATE/WRITE/READ workflow. The actual pinned CloudSoda integration binary
`cloud-upstream-tests` executes these **16 test functions per dialect**, not a
whole-suite claim: TestDirFS, TestGlobFS, TestSFMMount, TestSFUMount, TestReaddir,
TestFile, TestRename, TestChtimes, TestChmod, TestListSharenames, TestListShares,
TestServerSideCopy, TestRemoveAll, TestGlob, TestEcho, TestReaddirPlus. All named
subtests are retained in `logs/cloud-202.log`, `cloud-210.log`, `cloud-300.log`,
`cloud-302.log`, `cloud-311.log`: **80 function/dialect rows**, signing required.
`P0` is used for both configured client share aliases, so this external run does
not establish two-share isolation; the C# two-tree test does. The Restricted
profile can cause the client's copy fallback; this external TestServerSideCopy
pass does not establish server-side offload, which is checked separately with
CopyOnly. Other client-internal root tests were not run as server tests.
Go 1.22's automatic `go1.25` resolution first failed (`go-tidy.log`); explicit
`GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.25.0` succeeded (`go-tidy-1.25.0.log`). Authentication is **not**
blocked in these fresh runs. No Windows, Wine, crossbuild, full native OS rig,
Kerberos acceptor or whole-dialect conformance claim follows.

## First completed batch: pre-auth-repair results and serial handoff

The first completed source snapshot registers **79 cases: 50 filesystem/state and 29
authentication/framing/encryption cases**. These are executable case counts;
operation/table/dialect rows are stated separately and are not added to that count.
That snapshot’s Linux JIT: **73/79**, `logs/final-source-jit.log`. That snapshot’s Linux Native AOT:
**72/79**, `logs/final-source-aot.log`. The same six deterministic cases fail in
both; concurrent first-open also fails in AOT and in multiple earlier JIT logs.
JIT's intervening pass does not erase the observed race. No retries convert
failures to passes, no case is skipped, and no expected-failure conversion exists.

Both final builds compile cleanly; AOT retains pre-existing IL2026/IL3050 warnings
for unsupported JSON persistent-handle APIs. Logs include build identities and
loaded/executable artifact identities. `snapshots/before-build-sha256.json`,
`final-source-sha256.json`, `production-drift.json` and per-version owned source
snapshots identify the tested source. **Production drift during this original pre-repair phase is
empty**. Later authorized auth changes are captured in the separate phase below. Concurrent additions by other agents mean the entire checkout is not
claimed frozen. Pinned downloaded-source hash audit is also unchanged. Native
Windows remains unexecuted; no Wine or crossbuild substitute is claimed.

| Exact failing case | Observed RED / applicable expectation | Diagnosis and recommended small serial repair |
|---|---|---|
| `upstream.go.io.positioned-concurrent` | Intermittent CREATE returns `0xc0000043` SHARING_VIOLATION, expected success with all opens sharing read/write/delete. Seen in first-run, complete-run, final-jit (earlier 76-case version) and final-source-aot; final-source-jit happens to pass. | `Smb2Dispatcher` resolves a missing-path namespace key, waits for its namespace scope, then rejects when the first concurrent creator has published a stable object key. Reacquire/validate the changed namespace identity before backend mutation rather than returning a false share conflict. Preserve real share/rename conflicts and transaction rollback. Do not mask this with client retries or seed the file to avoid the race. |
| `upstream.go.io.truncate-invalid-preserves` | Signed `FileEndOfFileInformation=-1` yields `0xc0000033` OBJECT_NAME_INVALID, expected `0xc000000d` INVALID_PARAMETER. | Dispatcher reads the signed Int64 and calls the backend without a negative-value check. Validate this field before backend entry; preserve original data and allow the valid shrink retry. The field must be nonnegative under [MS-FSCC 2.4.14](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-fscc/75241cca-3167-472f-8058-a52d77c6bb17). |
| `upstream.go.readonly.new-file` | Read/attribute-only OPEN_IF of a missing name on `LocalFileStore(readOnly:true)` returns SUCCESS instead of ACCESS_DENIED. | Read-only guard treats OpenIf as nonmutating without checking existence. Refuse the missing-object creation path before acquiring a create-capable FileStream; retain successful read-only OpenIf on an existing file. |
| `upstream.go.readonly.mkdir` | Read/attribute-only directory OPEN_IF likewise succeeds on a missing directory. | Same guard gap reaches Directory.CreateDirectory. Apply the existence-aware read-only check to both directory and file acquisition. Other six read-only mutation cases pass; do not replace the guard with a blanket ban on reading existing files. |
| `upstream.go.auth.encrypted-ntlm-roundtrip` | Under RequireEncryption=true, successful initial SESSION_SETUP is a `0xfd SMB` transform rather than a plain `0xfe SMB` response. No encrypted file operation is reached. | `SmbConnectionHandler.EncodeOutbound` wraps every response addressed to Session.EncryptData, without the NEGOTIATE/SESSION_SETUP command exceptions. Apply [MS-SMB2 3.3.4.1.4](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-smb2/c4a91ca0-8d2e-404c-b9ac-3783ba9a01ef) at the outbound boundary while keeping required encryption on all applicable later traffic. The external Go encrypted configuration also times out in TestMain authentication before any selected test function runs. |
| `upstream.go.auth.encrypted-tag-tamper` | Same earlier required-encryption SESSION_SETUP failure; the intended corrupt-tag request is **unreached**. | Repair the common setup boundary first, then execute this case unchanged to reach tag validation under required encryption. It is not a second independent defect group. |
| `upstream.go.auth.encrypted-optional-tag-tamper` | After a valid independently encrypted exchange, one corrupted AES-CCM tag is silently dropped; the socket stays open until the bounded read cancels. Expected transport disconnect; the timeout remains a failure. | `DecodeInboundFrame` catches failed AEAD verification and returns null; the serving loop discards the frame and continues. Distinguish fatal authenticated-transform failures and request connection teardown. [MS-SMB2 3.3.5.2.1.1](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-smb2/94398d18-48ff-4b6c-a32d-0154b2e88238) requires disconnection for signature-verification failure. The separate optional-encryption roundtrip passes, independently checking the test's KDF/nonce/AAD/key-direction construction. |

Two exploratory read-only advertisement expectations were **withdrawn as oracle
errors**, not repaired in production or changed to match observed bytes.
`logs/final-jit.log` preserves the original 76-case run with those two failures.
The portable server hardcodes a reduced TREE_CONNECT MaximalAccess and a
read-only-volume flag. Here readOnly is a backend mutation policy over a writable
mounted volume: [TREE_CONNECT MaximalAccess](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-smb2/652e0c14-5014-4470-999d-b174d7b2da87)
is derived from the share security descriptor, while
[FILE_READ_ONLY_VOLUME](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-fscc/ebc7e6e5-4650-4e54-b17c-cf60f6fbeeaa)
describes a volume mounted read-only. Neither source choice is a mandatory result
of LocalFileStore's policy alone. Those two assertions are removed and explicitly
classified as normative mismatches. The independent read-only mutation failures
remain unchanged.

The required-encryption attempts are preserved in `logs/auth-expanded-first.log`
and `logs/encryption-first.log`; no setting was relaxed to turn those cases green.
Two distinct optional-encryption cases retain the original default host policy
and send encrypted packets voluntarily. The roundtrip passes; the tag case fails.
The known SPNEGO vector and accept-state assertions pass. The native and JIT
sources are the same final owned source, with no production edits between modes.

External client results remain **80/80 function/dialect rows** from the 16 named
CloudSoda tests on five dialects with signing required. The extra global encrypted
attempt is a **pre-test authentication blocker**, not 16 failed or passed tests;
`logs/cloud-encrypted-driver.txt` records its 23-second subprocess timeout and
empty client log. Future serial repair should rerun it after the plain
SESSION_SETUP boundary is fixed. Full native OS rig, Kerberos validator/realm,
POSIX/AAPL/DFS-specific backend features and client-only/internal cases retain
the explicit inventory dispositions below; they are not hidden behind that blocker.


## Post-auth-repair batch and current delivery

The first post-repair completed batch registered **82 cases: 53 filesystem/protocol
and 29 authentication/framing/encryption cases**. The current delivery adds one
distinct regular-file QUERY_DIRECTORY rejection and an unknown-share assertion
inside the existing routing case: **83 cases, 54 filesystem/protocol and 29 auth**. On the separately repaired
auth/session baseline, the 82-case Linux JIT and Linux Native AOT runs each pass **72/82**, with
**the same 10 failing cases**. Logs: `logs/post-auth-complete-jit.log` and
`logs/post-auth-complete-aot.log`. The earlier 79-case results above remain
historical RED evidence, not claims about this newer production baseline.

The separate owner changed the NTLM negotiator/parser and session state after the
original runs. This allocation made **no production edits**. Exact before/after
hashes are in `snapshots/post-auth-build-before.json`, `post-auth-build-after.json`,
`second-batch-before-build.json`, `second-batch-after-jit.json`,
`third-batch-before-build.json`, `third-batch-after-jit.json` and
`third-batch-after-aot.json`. The external post-repair builds/runs and current
82-case JIT/AOT builds/runs each have **empty production drift within their own
capture**. Owned final sources are saved with `complete-` prefixes in snapshots.
These hashes distinguish the changed baseline; the original unchanged-source
claim ends at the first completed batch.

Fresh external checks after that repair:

- Pinned hirochachacha v2 client, built with isolated Go **1.27.0**: before repair,
  all five signing-required dialect rows fail with `server did not negotiate
  requested signing` (`logs/hiro-202.log` through `hiro-311.log`). After rebuilding
  the server from the repaired source, all five pass authenticated
  CREATE/WRITE/READ (`logs/hiro-post-auth-*.log`). This independently verifies the
  narrow SIGN-bit repair. The exact raw-wire duplicate is
  `upstream.samba.auth.ntlm-negotiated-sign-flag`, documented in the
  [Samba allocation](upstream-samba-tests.md); it is not added again here.
- Pinned CloudSoda actual integration: the same **16 functions x five dialects =
  80 rows pass again** with signing required (`logs/cloud-post-auth-*.log`). No
  settings were relaxed. These are additional execution rows, not extra maintained
  tests, and not a whole upstream suite pass.
- Pinned hirochachacha actual integration: **32 selected functions on SMB302,
  24 pass / 8 fail / 0 skipped**, `logs/hiro-integration-post-auth.log` and
  `hiro-suite-selection.json`. The driver verifies a configured authenticated
  environment rather than accepting TestMain's silent unconfigured skip. All
  function/subcase outcomes are retained, including successful 18-row copy-offset
  subcases around individual failures; no failed function is reported passing.

The eight external failed functions are TestListShareNames,
TestMkdirPreservesReadOnlyPermission, TestOpenFileCreateExistingReadOnlyFile,
TestIsXXX, TestFileIdentity, TestClientBufferedCopyModel,
TestServerSideCopyOffsets and TestLargeFileCopy. They are not eight confirmed
mandatory server defects: the QFid context is optional/unimplemented;
credit-window failures are generated by the client before sending a request and
need separate compatibility analysis; Go permission projections are narrower
than portable SMB metadata guarantees. No error is retried away or silently
excluded from the external result. The feasible distinct public wire facets
are ported or cross-mapped as follows.

Three additional maintained regressions were run before any corresponding
production repair; all fail in both current modes:

| Exact case | RED evidence | Recommended small serial repair |
|---|---|---|
| `upstream.go.ioctl.response-buffer-offset-relation` | Real resume-key response has InputOffset=0, InputCount=0, OutputOffset=112; the mandatory rounded InputOffset+InputCount relation expects 0 from the declared fields, so the independent assertion fails. The stricter external client rejects the same serializer shape on srvsvc pipe IOCTL. | `IoctlMessage.BuildResponseBody` emits zero input offset but a nonzero output offset. Set the declared input-buffer base consistently with the fixed response end, preserving zero input count and bounded output. [MS-SMB2 2.2.32](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-smb2/f70eccb6-e1be-4db8-9c47-9ac86ef18dbb) makes the output relation mandatory even though InputOffset's choice is SHOULD. Reserved flags/FileId assertions remain after this first failure and are not claimed reached. |
| `upstream.go.names.open-if-existing-readonly` | Read/attributes-only OPEN_IF on an existing file made readonly by a preceding signed SET_INFO returns ACCESS_DENIED, expected success with unchanged data/attributes. | `CreateFileHandle` chooses FileAccess.ReadWrite for OpenIf even when the caller only requested read. Choose OS access from granted data access for an existing OpenIf object; retain create-capable access only when creating. Keep real write denial and do not chmod the file to make the open pass. Host readonly state is reset solely for fixture cleanup after the wire failure. |
| `upstream.go.metadata.create-directory-readonly` | CREATE response attributes and subsequent FileBasicInformation both return `0x10`, expected DIRECTORY|READONLY (`0x11`). | Apply supported requested CREATE metadata to newly created directories as well as files. The existing Samba file-attribute rows independently cover ordinary file CREATE/overwrite (`upstream.samba.attr.create.1`); this case adds the directory-specific public metadata facet. It does not require native Unix permission bits or promise POSIX ACL enforcement. |

The other seven current failing cases are the original positioned-open race,
negative EOF, two readonly-backend creation cases, two required-encryption setup

An additional intermittent defect remains even though the final 82-case runs
happen to pass its case: `upstream.go.enum.churn-300` failed in the first 81-case
run. Its original generic assertion is retained in
`logs/post-auth-second-batch-first-jit.log`. The only test change adds the actual
NTSTATUS to that diagnostic; it does not alter acceptable outcomes. One focused
check and **20 explicitly forensic trials** were retained, not converted into new
tests or used to supersede the original RED. Trial 12 reproduces
**OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND (`0xc0000034`) on QUERY_DIRECTORY of the still-existing
root while a child is renamed/deleted**, in `logs/churn-diagnostic-12.log`;
`churn-diagnostic-results.json` records all 20 outcomes. `LocalDirectoryCursor`
converts an enumerated FileSystemInfo to metadata after the child may vanish,
without handling that narrow race. Skip vanished child entries and continue the
cursor while preserving actual directory/access failures; do not suppress all
metadata errors. This is an eleventh observed failing case across the campaign,
not a claim that the current final run has eleven failures.

The new source's ordinary tests remain self-contained, offline, .NET10 JIT/AOT
and free of upstream runtime dependencies. No native Windows execution occurred.
All original artifacts and both baseline phases are retained; parent owns the
combined campaign report and serial production repairs.


The final inventory audit adds `upstream.go.protocol.enumerate-regular-file`
(the last distinct public subcase of Hiro's TestDirectoryEdgeCases) and checks
STATUS_BAD_NETWORK_NAME for the missing-share row of portable's scBadAuth inside
`upstream.go.routing.share-isolation`. No case is added for a client-only pathname,

**Final delivery: 83 cases. Linux JIT 72/83 (11 failures); Linux Native AOT
73/83 (10 failures).** The difference is the already-observed intermittent
`io.positioned-concurrent` first-open race. All ten other failures agree between
modes. The supplemental `enum.churn-300` failure remains independently observed

across these baseline phases, not twelve simultaneous final-run failures.

The last routing assertion also exposes a small protocol-constant defect:
`upstream.go.routing.share-isolation` reaches an unknown-share TREE_CONNECT and
receives **0xc00000be (STATUS_BAD_NETWORK_PATH)**, expected
**0xc00000cc (STATUS_BAD_NETWORK_NAME)**. The dispatcher selects its
`NtStatus.BadNetworkName` enum correctly, but that enum's numeric value is
3221225662 (0xc00000be). Correct that literal to 0xc00000cc for the
[MS-SMB2 missing-share response](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-smb2/652e0c14-5014-4470-999d-b174d7b2da87).
This is a mandatory status distinction, not a change of expected values to match
production. The regular-file QUERY_DIRECTORY rejection passes.

Delivery build/run evidence is `logs/build-delivery-jit.log`,
`logs/publish-delivery-aot.log`, `logs/delivery-jit.log` and
`logs/delivery-aot.log`. `snapshots/delivery-before-build.json`,
`delivery-after-jit.json` and `delivery-after-aot.json` show unchanged production
within this final build/run capture. Earlier snapshots and all first failures
remain intact. `delivery-summary.json`, `evidence-sha256.txt` and
`snapshots/delivered-owned-files-sha256.json` provide the machine-readable handoff.
No production repair belongs to this allocation; user edits and other agents'
files were preserved, and nothing was staged or committed.

There are also 19 named global parameter tables, three fuzz functions, 32
benchmarks, four TestMain functions, two examples and 30 matrix scenario callbacks
(the latter categories are already included in 1472). These are source census
counts, not adapted test or executed scenario counts.

## Exhaustive source function and subcase inventory

Disposition vocabulary: **adapted here**, **already covered** (named
local public assertions, subject to the independent audit qualifications), **unsupported feature**, **client-only semantics**,
**normative mismatch**, **external/platform blocker**, and **excluded internal-only**
(the explicit updated user exclusion). The later [independent audit](upstream-inventory-audit.md) found public facets hidden by some internal/client classifications and false exact mappings; its corrections below supersede those rows. Inventory disposition alone is not completion of every protocol facet. Groups with both protocol and private facets state
which facet maps and which does not. A mapping is not a pass; failing/unreached
assertions remain failing/unreached. TestMain, examples, benchmarks, scenario
callbacks and global parameter tables are listed separately from test counts.

The inventory below enumerates every function symbol with a pinned line permalink,
every named Run/step/each expression and literal table/range domain. Repeated
nested literals are deduplicated within a row. Global vector tables are listed
at their declaration and referenced by their original names. Long opaque binary
strings use length/SHA256 identifiers; immutable source links preserve exact bytes.
Named rows and numerical/boolean matrix domains are never replaced by a vague
“entire suite” claim. Numbered inline subcases are also retained. No generated
inventory is required to build or run normal tests.
